item.text: {"text":"NextItNet models item sequences using residual dilated causal convolutions, producing predictions across sequence positions. Its causality requirement suggests a direct prefix-invariance test: create two equal-length inputs identical through position t, perturb only later nonpadding tokens, and compare log2feats outputs at every position ≤t with torch.testing.assert_close. Run in eval mode with gradients disabled to eliminate dropout variation; repeat across cut points and dilation boundaries. Keep padding positions unchanged. Final-position scoring alone cannot establish causality because the final position has no future tokens to perturb; inspect earlier features directly. See the [NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf).\n\nFor diagnostic integration, register temporary forward hooks on the actual modules beneath view.model and count executions while running DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader). PyTorch hooks execute through module calls; directly calling a module’s forward method bypasses its registered hooks. Hooks can capture intermediate outputs or return modified outputs, and their handles support removal. A practical dependency-injection check is to construct the probe with the modified view, inject a controlled earlier-position fault, and verify that the prefix diagnostic detects it. This checks that the intended execution path is exercised; hook activation alone does not prove causal correctness. Use scoped hooks and remove them in finally blocks. These testing recommendations follow from the [PyTorch Module documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html)."}
